findings.title: The plan document still states, unannotated, the two premises this branch measured as false — that the guard cannot know whether a row would have been written, and that the two-read window is microseconds wide
findings.reason: The fix commit edited this file — it converted a stale line-range citation to a symbol citation and appended a 'SUPERSEDED IN REVIEW' note under the T2 bullet at line 106 — so the author's own convention here is to annotate a superseded claim. Three were left unannotated and are false at HEAD. (1) Lines 30-32, inside the normative 'Chosen shape (owner-approved)' section: 'The persist guard cannot know whether a row would have been written without running the resolver — which is the thing it exists to avoid.' The branch's own wouldRecordRefusal (persist.ts:723) disproves this, and every other artifact says so — arch-review-log clause (c), the guard-4 docblock (persist.ts:797-806), the runbook. (2) Lines 257-258: 'The window is synchronous and microseconds wide; it is the price of the pure predicate and is recorded as an edge case rather than defended against.' I re-derived the window myself: guard 4's read (persist.ts:850) reaches writeRefusalEvent's read (write.ts:443) via `await withLedgerAttribution(...)` -> `return await write();` -> the async arrow's body -> `await writeRefusalEvent(...)`, and an async call runs its body synchronously up to its own first await, so writeRefusalEvent's flag read — its FIRST statement — executes in the same run-to-completion segment as guard 4's. No suspension point exists, so no other task can flip the env between them. The window is ZERO, exactly what persist.ts:809-813 and the arch-review-log now say. (3) Lines 20, 23 and 77 keep 'PURE' as the contract word, which the branch retired repo-wide for SIDE-EFFECT-FREE precisely because vocabulary.ts:595 defines PURE in this feature area as excluding a flag read. Filed P1 rather than P0 deliberately: every AUTHORITATIVE surface (production docblocks, .claude/reference/arch-review-log.md, docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md, docs/reviews/fix-1079-.../review.md) carries the corrected version, and the plan is a superseded planning artifact. It is also the document a later reader opens first, and this branch exists because a retained claim in a superseded document was believed — escalate to P0 if the root judges the plan normative.

findings.title: The new accepted-findings checklist ships the REFUTED `some` predicate as forward-facing guidance to future async reviewers, with no correction
findings.reason: docs/reviews/finding-checklists/async.md is created BY THIS BRANCH and its own header says 'Reviewers on this axis receive this file and check the diff against every line' — it is a prescriptive input to future reviews, not a closed historical log. Its second entry states: 'blockReasons.some(c => Object.hasOwn(MAP, c) && MAP[c] !== null) is total, non-throwing, and returns false for exactly the empty and all-null-mapped sets write.ts:525-529 protects.' The clause after 'exactly' is FALSE and I have a machine-produced counterexample: with `.every(` replaced by `.some(` the property failed on ["policy_not_enabled","current_rating_missing"] — a MIXED set, one mapped and one null-mapped, that resolves to no row and on which `some` returns true. The integration half-B run refuted it a second time on live Postgres with the ['autopilot_tier_required','rating_below_positive_quadrant'] fixture. This is the single error the branch corrected most emphatically: persist.ts:807-812, write.ts:139-144, the arch-review-log row and review.md:69-74 all say `every`, never `some`. The one artifact a future reviewer is actually handed is the one that still says `some`. The file's own header restricts edits ('Lines are appended by review-log.mjs triage; edit only to prune entries that no longer apply'), so the remedy is a scope call for the root: prune the entry, append the correction, or accept the risk on the record.

findings.title: The new property's comment claims guard 4's length check is covered by the approved-draft cases; no test reaches that expression and deleting it survives 99/99
findings.reason: The comment reads: '`minLength: 1` keeps the empty set out of the generator; the "empty warns nothing" half is guard 4's length check and is covered by the approved-draft cases above.' The BEHAVIOUR is covered — an approved draft warns nothing — but not by the named mechanism, and the named mechanism is uncovered. An approved decision returns at guard 2 (persist.ts:845) and never reaches guard 4, so no approved-draft case executes `blockReasons.length > 0` at all. Measured, not reasoned: M-DROP-LENGTH survives 99/99 across the three touched suites (RT2-INV-08). The expression is in fact unreachable-as-false at its only call site — proof recorded on RT2-INV-08 — so believing the comment has no correctness consequence today, and that is why this is P1 and not P0. It is filed because it is the exact defect class the branch is about: a comment attributing an outcome to the wrong mechanism, sitting beside three carefully-corrected mechanism attributions. The honest wording is that guard 2 makes the length check defence in depth against a future guard reorder, tested by nothing.

findings.title: The guard docblock publishes '82/82' for guard 2 as a re-measurement 'against the CURRENT tests'; the current surface is 85 and the number is round 1's
findings.reason: The docblock says 'RE-MEASURED AT #1079, ONE AT A TIME ... re-ran that experiment against the CURRENT tests', then 'GUARD 2 — deletion SURVIVES, 82/82', and closes with 'Do not re-derive this; the numbers are the measurement'.
